en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on Sudhā (Sudhāvagga) 1.
The Apadāna of the Elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya.
If one honors those worthy of honor—
the Buddhas or their disciples—
who have transcended all conceptual proliferation (papañca),...
To those who have crossed over sorrow and lamentation—
to such as these, who have attained Nibbāna and are fearless from any quarter, one who offers worship.
It is not possible for anyone to calculate even this much merit,
even for all four continents.
If one were to exercise lordship over this world,
it would not be worth even a sixteenth part of the merit of making an offering to a single [Buddha].
At the stupa of Siddhattha, the supreme among men,
amidst the flowering trees,
a lump of lime was offered by me.
With a mind that was perfectly serene,
I performed that deed back then, ninety-four aeons ago.
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of reflection.
In the thirtieth aeon from now,
Known as the Paṭisaṅkhāra kings,
they were thirteen wheel-turning monarchs endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges,
these eight liberations,
and the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya recited these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya.
